scenes.narration: Before nineteen fifty-six, loading a single merchant vessel required hundreds of dockworkers hauling loose sacks and wooden crates one by one. Ships spent half their lives sitting idle in port, making international trade slow and prohibitively expensive.

chart.title: Port Loading Cost Per Ton (1956 vs Containerized)

scenes.narration: When trucking entrepreneur Malcom McLean introduced standardized steel containers that cranes could lift directly from trucks onto ships, port loading costs plunged from five dollars and eighty-six cents per ton down to just sixteen cents—a ninety-seven percent collapse.

Within two decades, global ports rebuilt around automated gantry cranes and intermodal rail links. That single logistics breakthrough turned isolated regional factories into today's interconnected global supply chain.
